$comment: The vocabulary of the OpenAMS UI, one fixed translation per language for every recurring term (PRINCIPLES.md 5, UNIFIED_UI.md 12). Read this before translating a string: the term's row is the only translation any of its ids may use, so 'spool' is the same word in the tile tag, the message row, the spool editor and the dryer form. 'tag' is the form used where the full word does not fit (the tile tag, a chip, a tile line, a header title) and is the same for every language, so the tags stay the same size as the English ones; it is a short form, not a second name. 'short' holds the same idea per language, for the languages whose full word does not fit the box English drew (round 2: the runout word grew in most languages, so most of them need a tag form). The ten translations live in design/strings/<code>.json.
never_translate: T0/T{n} - a tool is named by the slicer's own id
config names - oams1, oams2, A1, B2, HT-A
materials - PLA, PETG, ABS, PA, TPU, PC, ASA
products and brands - Spoolman, OpenAMS, AMS
RH - the relative-humidity symbol, as in '% RH'
the bare marks - ? and ∞, and ∞1/∞2 with it

short.$comment: Round 2, CORRECTIONS item 3: a term whose full word no longer fits the box English drew is recorded here as a short form. A short form is not a second name - it is the same term, cut to fit - so it must still be unambiguous on its own, and it is the only form the tile tag (TAG_*) may use. Each entry below exists because the language's full word was measured and did not fit at 1200px or 360px; every other language uses its full term in the tag unchanged.
short.$note_runout: German Ende (of filament) and Russian кончился (has ended) replace the literal 'runout' noun, which is longer in both. Japanese 切れ is the last character of フィラメント切れ, cut to one character for the tag; the full form still appears in STATUS_RUNOUT and the message rows. Polish Brak means 'not there', which is the state the tag reports. Korean 소진, Chinese 耗尽, Spanish Agotado, Portuguese Esgotado, French Épuisé and Italian Esaurito all fit the tag as their normal word and are not short forms.
short.$note_positioning: German is in progress here: the full Wird positioniert does not fit, so the tile tag takes the participle Positioniert and the message row keeps the full sentence. The other languages take a noun or a plain participle in the tag (French Position, Italian Posizione, Russian Позиция) where English uses the gerund; this is a known deviation, kept because their in-progress forms are longer than the tag and the tile context already says the motion is under way.
short.$note_environment: The device's menu tile (MENU_ENV, English 'Env') holds one short word: Russian uses Климат there and in the screen title (SCREEN_ENV): Среда alone reads as Wednesday first, and Окружающая среда means the natural environment.

$note_ru_bind: Russian keeps three concepts apart (principle 5): привязка is tool mapping (the menu tile fits it), закрепить is binding this display to a unit, and связать / связанная / отсоединить is a Spoolman spool's link.
round2: The cells below were checked against the localized UIs of Bambu Studio, OrcaSlicer, PrusaSlicer, Creality Print, Mainsail and Fluidd. Three recommendations the owner declined: Italian 'tool' stays strumento (estrusore is already 'extruder', and principle 5 forbids two concepts sharing one word), Chinese 'unit' stays 单元 (设备 also means the printer), and German 'alert' stays Meldung (the list mixes errors and information, which Warnung would not). Spanish 'mapping' is asignación, not the research's mapeo: mapeo and impresión both pull the screen toward 2D printing, which this screen is not.
